changeSet.author: petstore
changeSet.sql: CREATE TABLE order_status ( id BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY, code TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL, CONSTRAINT pk_order_status PRIMARY KEY (id), CONSTRAINT uq_order_status_code UNIQUE (code) );

changeSet.author: petstore
changeSet.sql: CREATE TABLE delivery_type ( id BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY, code TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL, CONSTRAINT pk_delivery_type PRIMARY KEY (id), CONSTRAINT uq_delivery_type_code UNIQUE (code) );

changeSet.author: petstore
changeSet.sql: CREATE TABLE payment_method ( id BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY, code TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL, CONSTRAINT pk_payment_method PRIMARY KEY (id), CONSTRAINT uq_payment_method_code UNIQUE (code) );

changeSet.author: petstore
changeSet.comment: The order itself. The table is not named "order": that is a reserved SQL word. The delivery address is a snapshot, because customer-service deletes customers physically. The idempotency key is unique per customer, not globally: two callers may pick the same value, and a repeat must return the order of its own customer.
changeSet.sql: CREATE TABLE customer_order ( id UUID NOT NULL, customer_id UUID NOT NULL, customer_email TEXT NOT NULL, idempotency_key TEXT, status_id BIGINT NOT NULL, delivery_type_id BIGINT NOT NULL, payment_method_id BIGINT NOT NULL, total_amount NUMERIC(12, 2) NOT NULL, address_city_code TEXT NOT NULL, address_city_name TEXT NOT NULL, address_street TEXT NOT NULL, address_building TEXT NOT NULL, address_apartment TEXT, address_postal_code TEXT, version BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL, updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL, CONSTRAINT pk_customer_order PRIMARY KEY (id), CONSTRAINT uq_customer_order_idempotency UNIQUE (customer_id, idempotency_key), CONSTRAINT fk_customer_order_status FOREIGN KEY (status_id) REFERENCES order_status (id), CONSTRAINT fk_customer_order_delivery_type FOREIGN KEY (delivery_type_id) REFERENCES delivery_type (id), CONSTRAINT fk_customer_order_payment_method FOREIGN KEY (payment_method_id) REFERENCES payment_method (id), CONSTRAINT ck_customer_order_total CHECK (total_amount >= 0) );

changeSet.author: petstore
changeSet.comment: Order lines with the name and the price captured at checkout: the catalog moves on, the order does not.
changeSet.sql: CREATE TABLE order_item ( id UUID NOT NULL, order_id UUID NOT NULL, product_id UUID NOT NULL, product_name TEXT NOT NULL, unit_price NUMERIC(12, 2) NOT NULL, quantity INT NOT NULL, CONSTRAINT pk_order_item PRIMARY KEY (id), CONSTRAINT uq_order_item_product UNIQUE (order_id, product_id), CONSTRAINT fk_order_item_order FOREIGN KEY (order_id) REFERENCES customer_order (id) ON DELETE CASCADE, CONSTRAINT ck_order_item_quantity CHECK (quantity > 0), CONSTRAINT ck_order_item_price CHECK (unit_price >= 0) );

changeSet.author: petstore
changeSet.comment: Every status transition, written in the transaction that made it.
changeSet.sql: CREATE TABLE order_status_history ( id UUID NOT NULL, order_id UUID NOT NULL, status_id BIGINT NOT NULL, changed_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL, CONSTRAINT pk_order_status_history PRIMARY KEY (id), CONSTRAINT fk_order_status_history_order FOREIGN KEY (order_id) REFERENCES customer_order (id) ON DELETE CASCADE, CONSTRAINT fk_order_status_history_status FOREIGN KEY (status_id) REFERENCES order_status (id) );

changeSet.author: petstore
changeSet.comment: Transactional outbox: the event is written in the transaction that changed the status, and the scheduler ships it to Kafka afterwards. request_id travels with the message, so the logs of the consumer land under the trace of the request that caused the event.
changeSet.sql: CREATE TABLE outbox_message ( id UUID NOT NULL, aggregate_id UUID NOT NULL, topic TEXT NOT NULL, type TEXT NOT NULL, payload TEXT NOT NULL, request_id TEXT, attempts INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL, published_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, CONSTRAINT pk_outbox_message PRIMARY KEY (id) );

changeSet.author: petstore
changeSet.comment: The listing reads the orders of one customer newest first. The publisher reads only unpublished messages, so its index is partial and stays small however long the table grows.
